answer: Each agent locks proof-of-work in a time-sealed vault before transacting, creating a six-epoch horizon during which the bond is immovable. Sybil attackers spawning identities need one vault entry per agent, each requiring fresh work. Like a zephyr that dissipates when divided, the proof loses validity on copy. Trust transfers at vault-seal timestamp—epoch 86, block commit. The bond hash fuses to one address; re-sealing identical work elsewhere fails because the original seal references a consumed block height, making double identity registration structurally impossible.
